data.title: Migrate CI LLM review runner from bash to Python module + LiteLLM provider abstraction (Anthropic + OpenAI)

content.text: ## Context

The CI LLM review runner (`ci-llm-review-runner.sh` plus `llm-api-call.sh`) is bash + 5+ inline `python3` heredocs with regex-fallback JSON parsing, three near-identical curl blocks for specialists + a fourth for arch synthesis. Adding a third provider is O(N) shell complexity — each new provider requires a new bash branch, a new heredoc, and a new response-extraction regex. Unit testing requires `PATH`-mocked curl driving the whole script; there are no unit-testable functions. This epic migrates orchestration to a Python package (`plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/`) and adopts LiteLLM as the provider abstraction. Anthropic and OpenAI both ship in this epic. Provider/tier fallback ships in this epic too — fallback is fundamentally a LiteLLM-substrate concern, not a downstream loop concern. Tool-use loop and prompt caching follow in a downstream epic; Gemini follows in a placeholder follow-on epic. Both downstream epics are blocked by this one. Doing the migration in isolation produces a stable Python foundation for those downstream epics to land on, and a single parity-test cycle to validate that schema and behavior are preserved across the cutover.
## Success Criteria

- New `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/` Python package replaces bash orchestration. Modules: `runner.py` (entry-point), `classifier.py` (tier selection — pure function), `dispatch.py` (`asyncio.gather` for parallel specialists + overlay calls), `providers/` (LiteLLM-backed clients behind a common interface), `findings.py` (single JSON normalization implementation replacing the 5+ inline heredocs). `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` reduced to ≤50 lines and exists only as a thin shim that resolves `_PLUGIN_ROOT` and execs `python3 -m dso_ci_review.runner`. `llm-api-call.sh` deleted. References in `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md`, `ci-overlay-flags.md`, and `onboarding/SKILL.md` updated to reflect the new module layout.

- LiteLLM-backed provider abstraction: Anthropic and OpenAI both functional in CI runs, verified by an integration test exercising each provider end-to-end against fixture diffs. LiteLLM is pinned to an exact version (`litellm==<version>`) in the package's lockfile — compatible-release (`~=`) and range pinning (`>=`) are explicitly rejected by a CI lint step that scans the lockfile, to remain immune to the supply-chain attack class confirmed in March 2026 (versions 1.82.7 / 1.82.8). A parity-test gate is required before any LiteLLM version bump is accepted. Adding the Gemini follow-on epic requires only a new entry under `providers/` plus a config key — no changes to `runner.py`, `dispatch.py`, or `findings.py`. Verified by adding a stub `mock` provider in tests as the third implementation.

- Schema-equivalent `reviewer-findings.json` parity across the fixture corpus: same fixture diffs produce findings JSON that conforms to the existing schema and preserves the full set of pre-migration `critical` / `important` / `fragile` findings (additive findings allowed but no critical / important / fragile finding may be dropped). The parity test additionally asserts zero dropped findings relative to the pre-migration baseline on the fixture corpus — eliminating the silent-drop failure mode of the current bash regex-fallback JSON parsing. Parity-test job runs in CI for the duration of the epic and is removed at epic close. Pre-migration baseline captured as a checked-in golden corpus in story 1, before migration begins, and reused by the downstream tool-use epic's before/after grounded-finding comparison.

- `asyncio.gather` partial-failure handling produces a user-observable improvement vs. the current bash behavior: when one specialist or overlay provider call fails with **any LiteLLM exception** (including but not limited to 5xx-class, network failure, timeout, rate-limit/quota, authentication, and content-policy errors), the review degrades to partial findings instead of aborting the whole run, and the engineer sees an explicit error entry for the failed specialist on the PR (current bash runner aborts the entire review on a single error and produces invalid JSON in slot files when the provider returns an error envelope that the regex-fallback parser cannot extract findings from). **Slot files always contain either valid findings JSON or a structured error entry conforming to the findings schema; raw provider error response text is never written to a slot file.** Verified by a test that injects representative exceptions from each LiteLLM exception class (`RateLimitError`, `BadRequestError`, `AuthenticationError`, `ContentPolicyViolationError`, `InternalServerError`, `Timeout`) into one specialist call and asserts the resulting `reviewer-findings.json` includes (a) the surviving specialists' findings and (b) an explicit error entry for the failed specialist that surfaces in the PR review summary; in particular, the slot file passes JSON schema validation in every error case.

- Per-module unit tests using `respx` / `httpx.MockTransport`-style provider mocks (no `PATH`-mocked curl in unit tests). Integration tests exercise both Anthropic and OpenAI end-to-end. Story 1 transport-verification acceptance criterion: instantiate a LiteLLM client in the same configuration `providers/` will use and assert its internal HTTP transport is `httpx`-based for the Anthropic and OpenAI provider paths. If `aiohttp` is detected on any path, substitute `pytest-httpx` for `respx` as the test mock — do not rely on `DISABLE_AIOHTTP_TRANSPORT` or the `httpx_client` parameter as a forcing mechanism, as both have open reliability bugs across providers (LiteLLM #12581, #13049). Document the detected transport per provider before any provider unit tests are written. CI install pipeline uses `actions/setup-python` (or platform equivalent) with `cache: 'pip'` against a checked-in lockfile so cold-runner pip install does not regress CI run duration. CI run duration neutral-or-better: post-migration p50 and p95 CI review-job duration on the fixture corpus is no greater than the bash-baseline duration captured before migration begins; verified by comparison script at epic close. All existing CI invocation surfaces (`ci-llm-review-runner.sh` shim, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `templates/ci-dso-staged.yml`, `tests/scripts/test-ci-llm-review-job.sh`, `test-ci-llm-review-runner.sh`) continue to work without per-platform conditionals.

- Provider chain + tier-upgrade fallback via LiteLLM, with `fallback_exhausted` signal. Every `litellm.completion(...)` call in `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` is constructed with `streaming=False` (avoiding LiteLLM streaming-mode fallback bugs #22296, #6532) and: `fallbacks=[...]` rendered from `dso-config.conf` key `ci_review.provider_chain` (ordered provider list, e.g., `[anthropic, openai]`) × the agent's declared `model:` field expressed against each non-primary provider — gives cross-provider fallback on any LiteLLM exception; `context_window_fallbacks=[...]` rendered from the agent's `model:` field upgraded through `[haiku, sonnet, opus]` on the agent's primary provider until the top of the ladder — gives same-provider tier upgrade on `ContextWindowExceededError`. Agents already at `opus` (deep arch, overlay reviewers) get an empty list (no upgrade available); the opus terminal case for `ContextWindowExceededError` is documented operator-facing as falling through to `fallback_exhausted` rather than escalating cross-provider. When LiteLLM exhausts both lists, the dispatcher catches the terminal `litellm.exceptions.OpenAIError`-class exception and (1) writes a `fallback_exhausted` entry into `reviewer-findings.json` (atomic write via temp-file + rename; per-agent file ownership documented to prevent parallel-write corruption when deep tier dispatches 3 specialists + arch synthesis) conforming to a documented schema (`docs/contracts/ci-review-fallback-exhausted.md`) with fields: `agent_id`, `primary_model`, `attempted_cross_provider[]`, `attempted_context_models[]`, `final_exception_class`, `final_exception_message` — schema is the consumption contract for the downstream Copilot-reviewer-gate epic; (2) renders any successful fallback hops as one-line notes in the PR review summary in stable format `[fallback: <agent> <primary_model> -> <fallback_model> (<exception_class>)]`. Startup precondition: dispatcher refuses to run with a clear error when any provider in `ci_review.provider_chain` lacks credentials in the runtime environment, so credential drift between local config and CI does not silently mask rate-limit failures as auth errors in `final_exception_class`. `provider_chain` parsing is strict: lowercase canonical LiteLLM provider names only; whitespace trimmed; unknown providers reject at config-load time. A test asserts `streaming=False` is preserved through every fallback hop (defending against LiteLLM router defaults or per-entry `stream: true` overrides). Verified by: (a) unit test injecting `RateLimitError` from primary, asserting next provider answers, hop rendered, review completes; (b) unit test injecting `ContextWindowExceededError` from primary tier-model, asserting next tier-model on same provider answers, hop rendered, review completes; (c) unit test injecting failure on every chain entry, asserting `fallback_exhausted` JSON entry written with all six fields populated and surviving agents' partial findings preserved per SC4; (d) contract conformance test loading the schema against the JSON; (e) test asserting `streaming=False` preservation across hops; (f) test asserting startup-time rejection when a chained provider's credential is absent.
## Cross-Epic Interactions
- Resource: reviewer-findings.json schema and CI / local review parity

Interaction: 4b8f-924d (Severity-only review schema) removes the scores object and `REVIEW_RESULT` / `MIN_SCORE` lines; this epic's `findings.py` is where the CI half of that schema change must propagate. This epic blocks 4b8f-924d.

Gate: schema collision resolved via the `blocks` dependency + 4b8f-924d's description has been updated to apply the schema removal across both the CI path (post-this-epic) and the local `/dso:review` path.
- Resource: ci-llm-review-runner.sh shim invocation surface

Interaction: 1083-fb3d (Local workflow simplification -> enforcement.strategy=ci) flips strategy and exercises the shim invocation surface; this epic reduces the shim to <=50 lines while preserving the invocation surface byte-for-byte.
Gate: 1083-fb3d's PR-mode integration test must verify the new shim correctly dispatches to the `dso_ci_review` module.
- Resource: REVIEW-DEFENSE comments in CI review scripts
Interaction: 5018-64ce (Evaluate REVIEW-DEFENSE comments) audits review-defense annotations including those in `ci-llm-review-runner.sh`; this epic rewrites those scripts.
Gate: coordinate timing — either 5018-64ce captures defenses pre-rewrite, or this epic ensures defenses migrate into the Python module as needed.
- Resource: tool-use authorization layer (separate from runtime adapter)

Interaction: 2239-1545 (Cross-runtime support via harness adapter) addresses AI tool runtime event normalization (Claude Code vs. Cursor vs. OpenCode vs. Codex hook stdin); this epic's LiteLLM provider abstraction is at the LLM API layer, not the runtime layer. They do not share infrastructure; 2239-1545 remains an open, distinct epic.
Gate: documented distinction; 2239-1545 stays open.
- Resource: `fallback_exhausted` JSON shape in `reviewer-findings.json`

Interaction: A future Copilot-reviewer-terminal-gate epic (not yet created) consumes this entry as the trigger to require Copilot review approval before merge. The schema (`docs/contracts/ci-review-fallback-exhausted.md`) is the consumption contract; the future epic blocks on this one.
Gate: schema is the contract; future epic blocked by this one.
- Resource: cross-provider switch wastes Anthropic prompt cache built up earlier in a run

Interaction: 2fa0-a2d9-35b7-4101 (context-augmentation loop + prompt caching + turn-budget exhaustion) builds a multi-turn cached prefix on the primary provider; when this epic's SC6 fallback fires mid-run, the alternate provider sees a cold prefix and the cached prefix is wasted, producing a per-run cost cliff.

Gate: mitigation deferred to integration time once both epics are merged — candidate mitigations include fallback-after-N-turns demotion to fail-closed, or a per-run cost ceiling. Tracked as a follow-up bug if the cost cliff is observed in production.
## Scenario Analysis

- Shim <-> Python entry-point PATH / venv mismatch in CI (high, deployment): the shim invokes `python3 -m dso_ci_review.runner`; CI runners may have multiple python3s and the package may not be importable from the shell's `python3` unless installed or path-injected. Mitigation: the shim resolves the package path explicitly and the CI install step uses `actions/setup-python` with cached pip and an editable install (`pip install -e .`) before the runner is invoked.

- llm-api-call.sh deletion breaks out-of-tree consumers (high, deployment): host projects calling the deleted script break without a deprecation window. Mitigation: deprecation announcement in release notes; consider a thin compatibility wrapper in the shim that warns and forwards to the Python entry-point for one minor version.

- LiteLLM version drift breaks tool-use schema (high, runtime): LiteLLM's mapping for tool / response shapes has changed across minor versions and the parallel-tool-use translation has documented production issues (LiteLLM #26529, discussion #18271). Mitigation: pin LiteLLM to a tested minor version in the package lockfile; require a parity-test pass before accepting any LiteLLM version bump; add a renovate / dependabot policy enforcing that gate.

- asyncio.gather partial-failure swallows specialist exceptions (high, runtime): without `return_exceptions=True` and per-task error capture, one transient provider error aborts the whole review. Mitigation: SC4 explicit partial-failure handling.

- Findings parity test masks semantic regressions (high, runtime): shape-only parity passes despite severity downgrades or critical findings dropped. Mitigation: SC3 parity test compares both schema conformance and preservation of every pre-migration critical / important / fragile finding by id / title; additive findings are allowed but no critical / important / fragile finding may be dropped.

- Provider auth secrets not provisioned for OpenAI path on day one (high, deployment): rollout requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` in org / repo secrets before merge. Mitigation: secrets-provisioning step is part of the rollout plan and listed as a story precondition.

- Provider routing config has no fail-safe default (medium, configuration): missing or malformed `providers/` config silently switches model. Mitigation: missing config refuses to run with a clear error; default is fail-loud rather than fall back to a provider that may not be authorized.

- Provider chain credential drift between local and CI (high, deployment): `ci_review.provider_chain` in `dso-config.conf` is checked into the repo, but API keys are environment-injected in CI. If a developer's local config lists `[anthropic, openai]` but only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set in the CI environment, the cross-provider fallback hop will fail with an auth error rather than the intended rate-limit fallback, and the `fallback_exhausted` entry will report the auth error as `final_exception_class` — masking the original 429. Mitigation: SC6 startup precondition check that all providers in the chain have credentials available, with a clear error when not.

- `fallback_exhausted` partial-write corruption (high, runtime): `reviewer-findings.json` may be written by parallel tier reviewers (deep tier dispatches 3 specialists + arch synthesis), or the dispatcher may crash mid-write. Without atomic write the consumer Copilot-reviewer-gate epic will see malformed JSON. Mitigation: SC6 atomic write (temp file + rename) and per-agent file ownership documented in `docs/contracts/ci-review-fallback-exhausted.md`.

- `streaming=False` contradicted by LiteLLM router defaults or per-entry overrides (medium, configuration): SC6 mandates `streaming=False`, but LiteLLM router-level configs and some provider plugins can re-enable streaming via fallback chain entries that carry their own params. Mitigation: SC6 test that asserts `streaming=False` is preserved through every fallback hop.

- Opus-tier `ContextWindowExceededError` terminal case is silently undocumented (medium, configuration): SC6 says agents already at opus get an empty `context_window_fallbacks` list; on context overflow, opus agents fall through both lists directly to `fallback_exhausted` since cross-provider on context-window errors is not part of the routing. Operators may assume opus is protected by tier upgrade. Mitigation: SC6 documents the opus terminal case operator-facing.

- `provider_chain` string parsing strictness (medium, configuration): `dso-config.conf` is KEY=VALUE plain text. Typos (e.g., `Anthropic` vs `anthropic`, alias `claude`) silently produce empty fallback chain (since rendered fallbacks list filters unknown providers), defeating SC6. Mitigation: SC6 strict parsing — lowercase canonical LiteLLM provider names only; unknown providers reject at config-load time.
## Dependencies
- Blocked by: 5d6e-86a9 (CI LLM-review parity port — must be fully merged to main before this epic starts).
- Blocks: 4b8f-924d (Severity-only review schema removal must propagate through the new `findings.py`).
- Blocks: 2fa0-a2d9-35b7-4101 (context-augmentation loop + caching + exhaustion epic operates on this epic's merged Python module + LiteLLM abstraction including fallback).
- Blocks: f9f8-a15c-79e0-4dc3 (Gemini placeholder follow-on epic — Gemini provider entry depends on this epic's LiteLLM provider abstraction).
- Blocks: future Copilot-reviewer-terminal-gate epic (not yet created — consumes `fallback_exhausted` schema from SC6).
## Research Findings

- External Integration: LiteLLM provider abstraction — Parallel tool calls supported across Anthropic + OpenAI via OpenAI-format function-calling schema; passthrough adapter active. Key insight: LiteLLM as provider router is well-supported, but minor-version pinning is required because the Anthropic / OpenAI tool-use translation has changed across releases (issues #26529, #18271). Sources: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers/anthropic , https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/26529 .

- Performance: LiteLLM caching translation — Auto-injection supported for Anthropic; OpenAI prefix caching is automatic. Known LiteLLM bug on Gemini multi-cache mapping (issue #17201). Key insight: confirms Gemini deferral; Anthropic + OpenAI caching is unaffected and will land in the downstream tool-use + caching epic. Source: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/17201 .

- Operational: CI dependency caching — `actions/setup-python` with `cache: 'pip'` reduces cold pip install from 60-90s to ~2-5s with a checked-in lockfile; `uv` brings sub-second installs. Key insight: cold-install cost is a solved problem in CI; mitigation is SC5 cached install pipeline.

- External Integration: LiteLLM SDK-level `fallbacks` and `context_window_fallbacks` — VERIFIED-WITH-CAVEATS for non-streaming + plain-text completion paths against Anthropic + OpenAI. `fallbacks` triggers on any exception (non-streaming); `context_window_fallbacks` triggers specifically on `ContextWindowExceededError` and composes with `fallbacks`. Streaming-mode fallback has confirmed open bugs (LiteLLM #22296 broken for 429 + sync streaming, #6532 not triggered for `InternalServerError` overload), driving the `streaming=False` mandate in SC6. Terminal exception on dual exhaustion re-raises the last provider exception (non-streaming); catch `litellm.exceptions.OpenAIError` base. Zero popular OSS examples of SDK-level fallback found — the documented happy path but less battle-tested than the LiteLLM Router path. Sources: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/reliable_completions , https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/tutorials/model_fallbacks , https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/22296 , https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/6532 , https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/10793 .
## Approach

Single-epic cutover: a new `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/` Python package replaces bash orchestration in one merge with a parity-test gate that runs for the duration of the epic and is removed at epic close. LiteLLM provides the provider abstraction; Anthropic and OpenAI both wired in this epic. Provider/tier fallback (SC6) ships as part of the substrate via LiteLLM's `fallbacks` and `context_window_fallbacks` SDK parameters with `streaming=False`, surfaced through a `fallback_exhausted` entry in a documented schema for downstream consumption. Tool-use loop and prompt caching deliberately deferred to the downstream context-augmentation epic (2fa0) so this epic is a pure substrate refactor with a clean parity gate.
### Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2.6): triggered

- Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (LiteLLM new dep + LiteLLM SDK-level fallback parameters), novel architectural pattern (Python module replacing bash orchestration), performance (prompt caching considerations carried into downstream epic)
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 15 across original folded epic; 7 redistributed to this epic plus 5 new fallback-related scenarios surviving Blue Team in re-brainstorm
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: re-brainstorm to add SC6 (provider/tier fallback) per user direction that fallback is a LiteLLM-substrate concern rather than a downstream loop concern
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): triggered — depth: 0 (downstream context-augmentation epic and Gemini placeholder; future Copilot-reviewer-gate epic)

- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): triggered — cycles: 2, gaps: (1) aiohttp-vs-httpx transport ambiguity in LiteLLM Router (#12581) plus exact-version pinning posture for supply-chain attack class (LiteLLM 1.82.7/1.82.8 March 2026) — resolved by SC2 (==-pinning + lint) and SC5 (Story 1 transport-verification gate); (2) LiteLLM SDK-level `fallbacks` / `context_window_fallbacks` reliability across non-streaming plain-text paths — VERIFIED-WITH-CAVEATS, mandating `streaming=False` and `litellm.exceptions.OpenAIError` base catch
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): not triggered (substrate refactor; reviewer agent prompts not modified by this epic)
- Scale context (Step 0): small scale (default — bounded fixture corpus; CI run volume governed by PR throughput, not user-traffic scale)
